examples.prompt:
I want to train my triceps but I have no gym equipment. All I have is two one-litre juice cartons.
Recommend one safe exercise and explain how to do it.

If nothing you know of trains that muscle with that object, say so instead of inventing one.
examples.gold:
Exercise: dumbbell tricep kickback with stork stance
Gym equivalent: dumbbell
Adaptation: Use two one-litre juice cartons in place of the dumbbells, one in each hand. Match the load on both sides so the movement stays symmetrical.
Steps:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in your right hand.
2. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
3. Bring your right elbow up to your side, keeping it bent at a 90-degree angle.
4. Extend your right arm straight back, squeezing your triceps.
5. Pause for a moment, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
6. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
Safety: Keep the movement controlled and stop if you feel pain.

examples.generated:
Exercise: dumbbell lying hip abduction
Gym equivalent: dumbbell
Adaptation: Use a duffel bag full of laundry in place of the dumbbell. Match the load on both sides so the movement stays symmetrical.
Steps:
1. Lie on your side with your legs extended and your arms by your sides.
2. Hold a dumbbell in your free hand with your palm facing down.
3. Keeping your upper arm stationary, lift the dumbbell out to the side, rotating your torso towards the opposite leg.
4. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
5. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
Safety: Keep the movement controlled and stop if you feel pain.
